newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen steady after in-line CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen steady after in-line CPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening steady, with a slightly lower bias, on Tuesday after a report on the May consumer price index met Wall Street expectations.
"The CPI data is a stable figure," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics.
"The Fed will be happy with this. Inflation is status quo despite all the ground the economy has covered. Stocks will likely open steady," he added.
The Labor Department reported the CPI rose 0.1 percent. Economists in a Reuter survey had expected a 0.2 percent increase.
The core CPI rate, minus food and energy components, was up 0.2 percent, in line with expectations.

"We did not expect any surprises from the CPI at this point, but I think all the good news on the CPI front has already been priced into the stock market," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at Boston-based Panagora Asset Management.
The 30-year Treasury bond was off 3/32, to yield 6.70 percent after the release of the data. The S&P 500 future dipped 1.3 points to 902.85.
